features.q: They agreed to remember the harvest they made together, not every shadow the river showed them.
Ever after, villagers taught their children that courage sends the first seed, fairness sends grain home, and kindness leaves enough on both shores to plant again next spring.

features.q: “What if he keeps the harvest?” she asked.

“What if he keeps the harvest?” she asked.

“Then he will eat once,” Mira answered. “If he shares, we can sow again.”
The river obscured her boat on its journey, but she did not send less because he might see less.
The spirit blew against the boat until its load seemed to disappear. Mira did not accuse the current or its keeper.

She could have counted the mist instead of the cargo, but she lifted each seed from the hull and planted it.
“A boat sent away empty may return empty.”

“A boat sent away empty may return empty.”

Mira answered, “It has returned before.”

“How can you repay what you cannot see?”

Mira lifted the seeds from the boat. “I can see what reached me,” she said, “and remember who sent it.”
Orin could have mistaken the reeds for an empty boat.
Orin could have mistaken the reeds for an empty boat. Instead, he hauled it ashore and found Mira’s gift.
“You could keep the season.”
Ever afterward, the villagers tied thread to their boats. It did not promise calm water or a harvest. It reminded each shore to trust the crossing and honor what arrived.

transitions.before_quote: The Ferryman returned enough grain that her gift had not been a loss, keeping enough to feed his family.
transitions.after_quote: He divided the harvest so that each bank would end the day with the same full granary.
transitions.summary: The endorsed return target shifts from preventing the giver’s loss to equalizing both granaries.
